9-panel cinematic storyboard sheet derived from Image 1. Mix Wide, Medium, and Tight shots of the same scene. No borders between panels.

Layout: 3x3 grid (9 panels) in a 16:9 landscape image.

Scene: Sun-drenched coastal cinematic still with modern social-first lifestyle beauty energy, 16:9, clean bright true-to-life color grading and warm natural skin tones, crisp whites and airy lifted shadows. Scarlett (Image 2) in oversized white linen button-down shirt worn loose and slightly open over light beige natural linen shorts, barefoot, stands mid-thigh in the shallow turquoise wash at Bondi Beach shoreline; a gentle wave has just broken near her so fine white spray mists her legs and the soaked hem of her linen shirt while she has finished dipping both hands into the cool water and is now raking wet fingers back through her free-flowing windswept hair, mid-gesture with wet linen clinging, water droplets flying, coral #D4536D lipstick still razor-crisp and vivid as she lifts her face into the salt air with a genuine unguarded smile breaking across her expression, potential energy held in the rising arms and sunlit salt spray. Behind her the open ocean rolls to a soft horizon under expansive bright sky, wet packed sand gleaming around bare feet with foamy edges, farther dry golden sand holding the left-behind towel and tan leather sandals as tiny out-of-focus anchors. Brilliant high morning sun sparks diamond reflections across the rocking water surface, strong rim light threading through the airborne mist and backlighting wet hair and translucent down cuff of the linen, clean directional fill keeping the moment high-key yet tactile with crisp foam texture and droplets frozen mid-air. Medium full-body shot slightly below eye level with soft anamorphic foreshorten and shallow depth of field, Releasing focus from sparkling foreground spray to the radiant figure then dissolving distant horizon, handheld micro-energy locked on the sensory peak, editorial cinema resolution, every highlight true and immediate.

Every panel is a shot of the same scene as Image 1 — keep the characters, wardrobe, lighting, color grade, and texture consistent across all panels.

No text, dialogue bubbles, scene numbers, or watermarks.

Reference images define identity — keep every referenced character, object, and location consistent with its reference image; never render a reference image itself as a separate panel or subject.
